HAM.name: Lewis Hamilton
HAM.text: Hamilton is known to be easy on tyres. He typically extends stints, manages rear degradation, and is less likely to cliff a set than more aggressive teammates.

VER.name: Max Verstappen
VER.text: Verstappen extracts high pace without usually destroying the tyre; he can push early in a stint and still hold a competitive long-run slope.

NOR.name: Lando Norris
NOR.text: Norris is balanced on tyres: competitive out-lap pace with average degradation, often the undercut reference versus Verstappen.

LEC.name: Charles Leclerc
LEC.text: Leclerc is often front-limited: strong qualifying, can grain the front-left on high-deg tracks if he pushes the entry too much.

RUS.name: George Russell
RUS.text: Russell is smooth on tyres and typically matches Mercedes long-run targets; useful as a one-stop candidate when the car is kind to rears.

PIA.name: Oscar Piastri
PIA.text: Piastri is clean on long runs and rarely overheats the rears; McLaren often uses him as the offset-strategy car versus Norris.

SAI.name: Carlos Sainz
SAI.text: Sainz can be heavy on rear tyres when rotating the car on throttle; stints sometimes come in a lap or two shorter than the team target.

ALO.name: Fernando Alonso
ALO.text: Alonso is easy on tyres and historically one of the best at extending a first stint to jump traffic after a safety car.
